page: Microsoft Azure F4as_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 4 vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, which yields a ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and vector extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 for accelerated mathematical and cryptographic routines. This configuration includes no local storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote block storage for persistence.

Performance profiles show strong single-core execution capabilities, reflected in top-tier results for stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, PassMark CPU tests, and Redis operations scales evenly across the 4 physical cores, landing within median industry ranges. Lightweight inference tasks on small language models demonstrate strong throughput during text generation, though processing throughput drops noticeably on medium parameter models due to the moderate core count and uncached write bandwidth of 34.51 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is driven by the dedicated core allocation without hyperthreading overhead, ensuring consistent CPU performance per allocated resource. Because the instance lacks bundled local storage, operational overhead depends on attached network storage. Microsoft Azure F4as_v7 is suited for compute-intensive workloads that rely heavily on single-thread frequency and vector execution, such as compression pipelines, microservices, batch processing, static web serving, and continuous integration runners.
description: Microsoft Azure F4as_v7 is a compute-focused instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 16.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets, it delivers top-tier single-core compute performance, as shown in compression and stress benchmarks. The VM includes no bundled local disks and no GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for disk operations. Memory throughput benchmarks show 52.65 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 34.51 GB/sec write bandwidth. Given the high clock rate and dedicated core layout, this server provides reliable compute density for batch data processing, compilation tasks, web serving, and mid-sized microservice workloads.
